item.title: Bandai Namco announced a narrower release window for the upcoming multiplayer-enabled brawler Dragon Ball Xenoverse 3, although it's not too much more specific. Previously, the publisher had stated that the sequel to 2016 fan-favorite would arrive in 2027. Now, it's turned that from a 12-month window into a six-month one, saying that it'll be out in the second half of 2027.
item.description:
Bandai Namco announced a narrower release window for the upcoming multiplayer-enabled brawler Dragon Ball Xenoverse 3, although it's not too much more specific. Previously, the publisher had stated that the sequel to 2016 fan-favorite would arrive in 2027. Now, it's turned that from a 12-month window into a six-month one, saying that it'll be out in the second half of 2027.
"Today we shared more information about battle customization and PvE missions," producer Masayuki Hirano said. "I wanted to use this opportunity to deliver a message to our fans. Over the past several months, we have continuously revealed new information to all of you and, in return, have received valuable feedback. We are truly grateful for that support. Based on the feedback and survey results we have gathered, we have already held discussions with the development team and announced certain areas where we intend to make improvements in response.
"Dragon Ball Xenoverse is a series that we build together with the players through launch, and throughout its post launch life as well," he continued. "To fully realize our ambitions for both the launch experience and the content we plan to operate and support afterward, the release window is currently set for the latter half of 2027." He concluded by suggesting that the team might stay quiet for a while now, saying, "We may keep you waiting a little longer until our next update, but we are fully committed to making 2027 a great year for Dragon Ball game fans, and we will do everything we can to make that happen."
IGN went hands-on with Dragon Ball Xenoverse 3 recently if you'd like to check out our preview impressions. Our first chance to play it was back in June.
Ryan McCaffrey is IGN's executive editor of previews and host of IGN's weekly Xbox show, Podcast Unlocked, and a co-host of Next-Gen Console Watch. He's a North Jersey guy, so it's "Taylor ham," not "pork roll." Debate it with him on Twitter at @DMC_Ryan.

Brandon Sanderson, author of The Cosmere books, has some thoughts on the new Mr. Beast book. More specifically, he is wondering who the true author actually is. During the latest episode of his podcast, Intentionally Blank, he decided to dive into his own perception of The Most Dangerous Games.
"I'm really curious who the ghost writer was," said Sanderson. "I would love for them to be credited, but I can see why they're not." He then goes on to explain how he personally goes about co-authoring books, which he recently did with Blightfall, and how he thinks that differs from being an editor. His final point on the matter was "if you see someone else's name on a book, chances are I came up with the outline and then was the editor on it."
For anyone who has followed Mr. Beast's YouTube career, it seems pretty unlikely that he did any of the writing himself. The fact that James Patterson is also listed on the book would make it seem the famous author is likely the one who did all of the heavy lifting to get this story off the ground. But Sanderson questions just how involved Patterson actually was in this project and if the true author is maybe left uncredited.
"Normally it's James Patterson and somebody," explains Sanderson, "what happens in those situations usually is James Patterson has an idea, they brainstorm and outline together, then the person writes the book and Patterson reads it and offers feedback."
"It doesn't feel like a James Patterson book," continues Sanderson. "but it's very strange for Patterson to use an uncredited ghostwriter, right?"
As someone who has helped finish The Wheel of Time Book series for Robert Jordan, Sanderson is no stranger to co-authoring a story. He admits later in the podcast that it's certainly possible that Patterson could have written the book, but he thinks an uncredited ghostwriter was definitely involved.
The book in question, The Most Dangerous Games, has been out since September and has received conflicting reports about its success. The official page for the book calls it "an unputdownable survival thriller". If you're interested in reading it for yourself, here's the description of the book:
"The Games begin in Antarctica, where one wrong step on the ice kills you, and they never let up: Shark water off a remote Chilean island, desert heat that cooks you where you stand, storm-battered peaks, and caves so black you cannot find your own hand. No rescue. No second chances. A billion dollars to whoever is still standing.
Then the terrain stops being the thing that can kill you, and the other players start. Alliances turn into ambushes. Trust becomes the sharpest weapon. And somewhere above it all, a hidden voice is watching every move, testing, deciding who deserves to survive."

item.title: One of the most iconic fast food restaurants from the GTA universe is becoming real ahead of GTA 6's release.
item.description:
One of the most iconic fast food restaurants from the GTA universe is becoming real ahead of GTA 6's release.
Rockstar Games' takeover of Miami is continuing to expand with a real-life version of Burger Shot, a famous fast-food restaurant in the GTA franchise. A fan on X shared the first images and info about the burger joint with GTA fan accounts, noting that it would be available at the Kaseya Center, which is the arena where the Miami Heat play.
It's unclear if the actual menu will be themed after the in-game restaurant, but it's sort of hard to imagine it will be. In GTA, Burger Shot pokes fun at fast food joints like McDonald's and Burger King for their extremely unhealthy meals. In the game, Burger Shot has menu items like "The Heartstopper," which features seven patties stacked high between a variety of toppings.
Miami's Kaseya Center has rebranded its burger restaurant as Burger Shot with Macca & Friends and Vice City posters also appearing inside the venue as part of #GTAVI's marketing campaign.Via @GTAVI_Countdown / @nvtnp_ https://t.co/FP3ly6kNen
It seems more likely that this is all purely decorative, but still, it's a fun touch. Additionally, leaks have indicated that Rockstar is also planning to sell some of the beer brands available in GTA 6 at bars in Miami. It's unclear if they will be available in retail stores or online for fans outside of Florida.
Rockstar Games has other ambitious plans for the Kaseya Center, including an unprecdented regular season game where the Miami Heat will turn into the Vice City heat for one night on November 18. The team will be given new jerseys and play on a GTA 6-themed court.
Rockstar has spent the last few weeks preparing for launch in Miami with extravagant marketing, which includes a $975,000 neon sign on top of the Kaseya Center that reads "Welcome to Vice City." Fans also recently spotted flashy GTA-branded sports cars driving around Miami. The cars were seen with camera crews, suggesting some kind of live-action advertising is happening for GTA 6.
We're officially less than a month away from launch, as GTA 6 will release on November 19 for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S. A PC version is also rumored to release early next year.
Cade Onder is a freelancer for IGN's news team. He covers all things entertainment, including gaming, film, and more. You can find him on Twitter @Cade_Onder.

item.title: Chris Pratt has confirmed that Star-Lord's return to the MCU is actively being figured out.
item.description:
Chris Pratt has confirmed that Star-Lord's return to the MCU is actively being figured out.
The beloved galactic hero has been absent from the MCU since 2023, but his last appearance ended with a promise during the credits: Star-Lord will return. When speaking with The Playlist, Chris Pratt was asked about Star-Lord's future. Pratt confirmed that Marvel has been having conversations about bringing back the character, but he's remaining tight-lipped on when that will happen.
“I have a great relationship with Kevin [Feige] and Lou [D’Esposito], and there have been both ongoing conversations about how we make good on that promise and also hard action taken to make sure that we make good on that promise,” he explained. “So yeah, you’ll see Star-Lord again, which is very exciting, but I’m not at liberty to say when that’s going to be, but he’s not going anywhere.”
Of course, Avengers: Doomsday is right around the corner and has a stacked cast... but Pratt is not among the list of confirmed stars. There are some actors who are heavily rumored to appear, but haven't been officially announced. However, Pratt hasn't really been part of the rumor mill. It's possible that he will be in the film's sequel, Avengers: Secret Wars, but we will likely have to wait until next year to know for sure.
Director James Gunn has been open about having no plans to do another Guardians of the Galaxy film, especially since he is now heading up DC Studios. Still, many of the characters he adapted for the big screen still live on in the MCU. Perhaps Star-Lord will get his own TV series. Maybe a solo film... or maybe he will return with a new crew in a potential Guardians of the Galaxy 4, helmed by another director. There are a ton of possibilities, but you can rest assured knowing Star-Lord is coming back.
Cade Onder is a freelancer for IGN's news team. He covers all things entertainment, including gaming, film, and more. You can find him on Twitter @Cade_Onder.

item.title: Prolific fighting game player SonicFox has terminated their contract with a tournament in Norman, Oklahoma after organizers fed artwork of their mascot character into AI to generate a promotional poster for the event.
item.description:
Prolific fighting game player SonicFox has terminated their contract with a convention in Norman, Oklahoma after organizers fed artwork of the pro's mascot character into AI to generate a promotional poster for the event.
SonicFox is one of the most successful fighting game players in the genre’s competitive scene. Known for being a multi-game specialist, SonicFox boasts multiple championships in a bevy of different titles, so it’s no surprise that they’re often invited as a special guest at tournaments across the United States.
One such tournament, taking place at a convention named Nexcon, invited SonicFox to attend alongside a few other notable guests. The convention is scheduled for November 14 - 15 in Norman, Oklahoma (home of the Sooners) — but now, SonicFox isn’t going to make an appearance.
On October 20, a concerned fan shared a promotional poster that Nexcon had made using generative AI on Twitter/X, which showed the likeness of SonicFox’s furry avatar, as well as the likenesses of other special guests, in an unmistakable AI art style.
“Not sure who’s in charge of Nexcon, but I absolutely refuse to have my likeness be AI-generated, and my interest in attending as a special guest has dropped to 0. Incredibly disrespectful,” the player replied.
It’s worth noting that much of the artwork SonicFox uses on their accounts is created by members of the furry community; feeding that artwork into a generative AI without their consent essentially steals their work to train on future models.
Not sure who’s in charge of Nexcon but I absolutely refuse to have my likeness be AI generated and my interest in attending as a special guest has dropped to 0.Incredibly disrespectful.
Members of the fighting game community spoke up in support of SonicFox, with one summing up the prevailing sentiments in a reply: “Using AI to help promote an event that gathers creators and artists is pretty crazy.”
A day later, SonicFox announced that they had terminated their contract with the event, saying in a simple post that they are “no longer attending.”
At the time of writing, all mention of SonicFox has been removed from NexCon’s website. Fans are speaking out in support of the pro player, with many congratulating them for “standing on business.”
In other fighting game news, Roger Jr. gameplay footage for Tekken 8 was shown off at Evo France, and players finally got a first look at Yujiro Hanma’s in-game model before his arrival early next year.

item.title: The Mass Effect video game franchise may have come to an end with the shocking demise of BioWare, but IGN can exclusively reveal that its future on the small screen remains possible. Sources inside Prime Video have confirmed that the Mass Effect television series remains in development at Amazon MGM Studios.
item.description:
The Mass Effect video game franchise may have come to an end with the shocking demise of BioWare, but IGN can exclusively reveal that its future on the small screen remains possible. Sources inside Prime Video have confirmed that the Mass Effect television series remains in development at Amazon MGM Studios.
Our source added that, as of now, all the creatives who were attached to the TV project remain onboard.
As of August 2025, Doug Jung (Mindhunter, Star Trek Beyond) was serving as showrunner with Daniel Casey (Fast & Furious 9) writing the series. The production team also included Jessica Jones executive producer Karim Zreik, BioWare's Mass Effect boss Mike Gamble, and former Marvel Studios boss Ari Arad.
The Mass Effect TV series has officially been in development at Prime Video since 2024, although it was first rumored back in 2021 after years of failed attempts to realize the sci-fi game franchise as a feature film.
We learned last year that the show won’t retread Commander Shepard’s origin story from the games and will instead be set after the original trilogy.
Daniel Casey took to social media this past April to shoot down reports that Prime Video wanted rewrites to make the show more appealing to a non-gaming audience.
The Mass Effect TV series had, at one point, been eyeing a Q4 2026 production start, but it remains without a release date as of time of this story’s publication.
Given the success of their Fallout TV series adaptation, Prime Video was reportedly hoping to capture lightning in a bottle twice with a Mass Effect show. IGN will keep you up to date on any further developments we learn.
In the meantime, read how the Internet reacted to the cancellation of Mass Effect 5 and the death of BioWare and our thoughts about how Mass Effect 5 was supposed to redeem the series after Andromeda (and now we’ll never get that).
Jim Vejvoda (he/him) is IGN's Assoc. Director of Entertainment Content.

item.title: Mark Darrah, who worked as an executive producer at BioWare from 1997 - 2021, shared his thoughts on the studio’s recent closure by EA and what he thinks might happen to its iconic IPs.
item.description:
Mark Darrah, who worked as an Executive Producer at BioWare from 1997–2021, shared his thoughts on the studio’s recent closure by EA and what he thinks might happen to its iconic IPs.
EA announced a major restructuring in a lengthy statement on October 21. Amid some exciting developments for Sims, Fight Night, and Star Wars fans came the devastating news that BioWare — the studio responsible for beloved series like Mass Effect and Dragon Age — was being shut down.
“As we focus on these larger opportunities, we've had a small team at BioWare working on early-development for Mass Effect. We've made the decision not to move forward with this development, which means we’re closing the studio and our Edmonton workspace. BioWare is a legendary studio that helped define the role-playing genre, and we do not take this decision lightly,” EA’s statement said.
This news hit the gaming world hard, with fans taking to social media to mourn the developer and send fired staff their well-wishes. But one burning question has risen above the sadness: What does this mean for the future of BioWare’s IPs?
Some fans have urged EA to sell them off to other companies, with CD Projekt Red being a big favorite due to the two studios’ close relationship over the years. And while nothing is certain, Darrah shared some insight as to what’s possible for BioWare’s creations in the wake of this devastating development — and it’s cautiously optimistic.
“Remember BioWare is 100% owned by EA,” he said in a YouTube video. “EA owns all the IPs. They own Dragon Age, they own Mass Effect, they own Jade Empire. That doesn’t change the situation, really, at all. …Now, there’s nobody working on a [BioWare] game, or games, within the EA organization, and chances are there never will be, which might make them more likely to sell off those IPs. But it might also make them more likely to just try to forget that they ever existed and bury them in the vault.
“I think we still are gonna have to wait a little bit before we see if EA has any interest in selling off some of its dormant IPs. Right now, they seem to be in cost control mode. They might start into a revenue-generation mode where selling IPs might be more desirable.”
It’s worth mentioning that EA was acquired by a consortium of private investors back in August in a mind-boggling $55 billion deal. As part of this acquisition, the investment group was reportedly banking on the hope that artificial intelligence might help cut costs to help manage its debt.
Given the investment group’s massive debt, some fans are curious to know if this means selling off some of BioWare’s beloved IPs to other developers — or perhaps back to BioWare under a different brand. For now, nothing is certain, other than fans and fellow game developers are equally beside themselves as they grapple with the news that Mass Effect 5 might never get made.

item.title: EA shut down BioWare earlier today, and fans of Star Wars: The Old Republic are paying their respects to the beloved developer.
item.description:
EA shut down BioWare earlier today, and fans of Star Wars: The Old Republic are paying their respects to the beloved developer.
Star Wars: The Old Republic was originally developed by BioWare, launching back in 2011. BioWare supported the MMO itself until 2023, when EA put Broadsword Games in charge of maintaining it. But the bulk of the game's story content was developed and written by BioWare, so it's little wonder that the SWTOR community would want to pay respects to the now-dormant studio following this latest news.
Reddit user WarlockingIn posted BioWare's farewell statement on the SWTOR subreddit, and in just a few hours, it's garnered nearly 5,000 upvotes and 742 comments supporting the now-defunct RPG developer.
Bae_the_Elf posted a comment, lamenting EA's treatment of the studio, saying, "RIP. One of the greatest gaming studios of all time in my opinion. Sad to see how corporate mismanagement and time sadly lead to the downfall of this studio. It would have been nice if they had just kept chugging out great RPGs at a steady pace for years."
Meanwhile, user AnnoyedYamcha was devastated by the closure, saying "NO. Not BIOWARE! They made so many great games. What the hell is going on!!! They were the bar for RPG's. KOTOR, MASS EFFECT, DRAGON AGE, JADE EMPIRE, they were all great! JADE EMPIRE though doesn't get enough love. I wish they made another. THANK YOU BIOWARE FOR EVERYTHING! 😭😭"
Some fans were surprised that SWTOR outlived BioWare, though. The top comment on the thread, from user Inangelion, simply says, "SWTOR outlives Bioware. What a strange timeline."
Some were even thankful that Broadsword took over, with user Dangerously_Stupid posting, "You know, a few years ago I was upset that BioWare was giving up SWTOR and handing it to Broadsword. I am no longer upset by that." Likewise, user KukiBreeze is just thankful that the MMO lives on another day, saying "Thank you Broadsword, a sh*tty day could have been 1000x sh*ttier otherwise."
Star Wars: The Old Republic fans aren't alone in mourning BioWare. People from across the internet have reacted to the studio's closure, and the fact that we'll never get a Mass Effect 5. But, for now at least, Star Wars: The Old Republic lives on, with hundreds of hours of peak BioWare storytelling.
Jackie Thomas is the Senior Tech Editor at IGN and the PC components queen. She's been covering gaming hardware for more than a decade for IGN, TechRadar, Gizmodo, PC Gamer and more. You can follow her @Jackiecobra

item.title: Quentin Tarantino penned the screenplay for The Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth, his follow-up to Once Upon a Time in Hollywood, but he handed the directing reins over to David Fincher – who proceeded to cut about 60 pages from Tarantino’s screenplay.
item.description:
Netflix has released a slew of new images from The Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth, which can be seen in the gallery below. Quentin Tarantino penned the screenplay for the film, which follows Brad Pitt’s former stuntman Cliff Booth in the years following Once Upon a Time in Hollywood.
But Tarantino isn’t behind the camera this time, handing the directing reins over to David Fincher – who proceeded to cut about 60 pages from Tarantino’s screenplay.
“The first draft I read was 230 pages. It was essentially two movies,” Fincher told Empire Magazine. “Somewhere in there was the Venn diagram of what Brad wanted to do, what I want to do, what Quentin wanted to do. Not ‘want to do,’ but the areas we would focus on.”
The trimmed down script nevertheless resulted in a movie that runs close to two hours and 20 minutes long.
Empire also interviewed Tarantino, who explained that his script for The Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth “was very different” from the one he wrote for Once Upon a Time in Hollywood. “To me, it had the flavor of an Elmore Leonard paperback: a crime-story paperback feel,” the Oscar winner said.
Fincher added that he “liked the idea that it’s a story around a bonfire. … It wasn’t about the plot as much as it was about how the participants collided with one another in the back alleys of Hollywood in 1977.”
Tarantino's full story for The Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth will be published as a novel this December and is now available to preorder.
The Pulp Fiction filmmaker also recently revealed that he’s written the screenplay for his 10th and final film, but wants to “live” a little before actually making it. In the meantime, Tarantino has penned a swashbuckler comedy stageplay titled The Popinjay Cavalier, which will be produced in London’s West End next year with Sacha Baron Cohen starring in the lead role.
The Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth opens in IMAX theaters globally on November 25, 2026 and launches on Netflix December 23, 2026. In addition to Brad Pitt, the film also stars Elizabeth Debicki, Scott Caan, Carla Gugino, Yahya Abdul-Mateen II, and Peter Weller.

item.title: EA has paused development on a mobile multiplayer Sims game in favor of moving forward with a rumored Sims 4 sequel.
item.description:
EA has paused development on a mobile multiplayer Sims game in favor of moving forward with a rumored Sims 4 sequel.
EA announced a wide variety of changes and projects today, including the closure of BioWare and the cancelation of Mass Effect 5. It also seemed to lean into recent rumors that DICE and Respawn are making a new Star Wars Battlefront game. One other big change is that EA is shelving a mobile-first multiplayer Sims project, formerly known as Project Rene and now known as Project Lotus. The game was once envisioned as the next big Sims title, but plans changed to more of a mobile spin-off once EA saw that people were still hanging on to The Sims 4.
With that game being put on the back burner, EA is shifting its focus to a Sims title that it's calling Project Evergreen. Although EA hasn't revealed what the focus of this game will be, rumors have been swirling about this project for a some time now. The game, which was rumored to be under the codename Project X, is expected to be a sequel to The Sims 4. Now, here's where it may get a bit confusing: It's not The Sims 5. It's being viewed more like The Sims 4 2.0. I know, it is unnecessarily complicated.
As covered by Sims Community, the project is reportedly targeting September 2027 as its deadline to go gold, suggesting the game would launch in fall 2027. The game will release on PC and is also expected to be optimized for portable handhelds, such as the Steam Deck. If it really is releasing next year, we will likely hear more about it at The Game Awards or sometime in the first half of 2027.
Earlier this year, the team behind The Sims hinted at a new single-player game in the franchise for PC and console, noting that half of its development team was working on The Sims 4 and its "next evolution."
Ultimately, this sounds like a win for fans who have been hoping for a new traditional entry in the franchise. The Sims 4 was released in 2014, meaning it has been 12 years since the franchise got a new game. There are a ton of updates and expansions that keep the game fresh, but building something from scratch and moving away from all the bloat could be a strong move for the future of the series.
Cade Onder is a freelancer for IGN's news team. He covers all things entertainment, including gaming, film, and more. You can find him on Twitter @Cade_Onder.

item.title: Deadline has confirmed that DC Comics’ Poison Ivy is in the early stages of getting her own live-action TV show, and one of the minds that brought us the critically-acclaimed Penguin series is in discussions to produce it.
item.description:
Deadline has confirmed that DC Comics’ Poison Ivy is in the early stages of getting her own live-action TV show, and one of the minds that brought us the critically acclaimed Penguin series is in discussions to produce it.
However, the outlet’s sources state that this show won’t be part of Matt Reeves’ Batman universe, so don’t get your hopes up for the chance of seeing Colin Farrell’s Penguin or Battinson sharing the screen with Dr. Isley.
Lauren LeFranc, showrunner and executive producer on HBO’s The Penguin series, is currently in talks to produce the Poison Ivy show. If it gets picked up, it’ll also go to HBO for streaming, but it’s still very early days for the project.
Right now, there are no writers attached to the series, and no cast has been revealed, either. It’s anyone’s guess as to who will get the leading role (Uma Thurman is a hard act to follow), but there’s plenty of freedom to be had, given that Poison Ivy is a character that hasn’t yet been represented in newer DC projects.
Thus far, she hasn’t shown up in James Gunn’s DC cinematic universe, and there’s been no word on the character’s involvement in the next Batman film. It’s worth noting that Scarlett Johansson is confirmed as part of the movie’s cast, sparking no end of fan theories as to who she’ll be portraying. While rumors suggest she's playing Harvey Dent's wife, Gilda Dent, many fan theories are hoping against hope that she'll be Poison Ivy. We have to admit that she would be a perfect fit for the DC anti-hero/villainess, and it would be a smashing debut for the actress in the DCU, following Black Widow’s exit from the MCU in Avengers: Endgame.
Poison Ivy’s most prominent appearance as of late has been in DC Studios’ animated Harley Quinn show, where her romance with her fellow villain takes center stage. It’d be exciting to see if this relationship is also included in the live-action series, and who will be cast as Harley Quinn if so. (Margot Robbie is most likely off the table with the new DCU reboot. Gunn himself has been rather coy about the whole thing, saying in August 2025 that Robbie's potential future in the DCU "will be revealed down the line.")
While they wait, fans can look forward to Clayface, which hits theaters on October 23. IGN’s Jim Vejvoda scored the film a 7 out of 10, saying it’s “a fun body horror romp that realizes its nasty potential in its final act after a slow-burn set-up.”

item.title: Prime Video has released a new trailer for the upcoming third season of The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power that revealed more of the war to stop Sauron from forging the One Ring.
item.description:
Prime Video has released a new trailer for the upcoming third season of The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power that revealed more of the war to stop Sauron from forging the One Ring. You can watch the trailer via the player above or the embed below.
Season 3 is set several years after the events depicted in Season 2, picking up the story at the height of the War of the Elves.
While the new trailer features more looks at the Nazgnagôl, a Mûmakil, and fell beasts, the best is saved until last when Sauron dons the One Ring, which will allow him to bind all the peoples of Middle-earth to his will.
“I see the path to victory so certain,” Sauron says. “I will take my place as a conqueror, a sorcerer. A king. We have work to do.” These lines are spoken over footage of a Nazgnagôl getting the upper hand of Galadriel in a fight. (Sauron also seems to be getting into Galadriel’s head at one point as she dreams that he’s lying in bed next to her.)
It also appears Sauron will battle the Balrog at some point this season as the trailer shows a fiery battle. (Simon Pegg voices the Balrog in the show.)
After the death of Celebrimbor in the Rings of Power Season 2 finale, Sauron is still seeking to forge the One Ring to rule them all as Season 3 begins. It would seem this season is going to see the Dark Lord come out on top in his quest to bring Middle-earth under his rule – well, for now anyway.
The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power Season 3 debuts on Prime Video on November 11. In the meantime, read up on the show’s mysterious new orc character and learn why the Harfoots won’t be in Season 3.
And also be sure to read our The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power Season 2 finale review and our spoiler-filled Season 2 ending explained and how it sets up Season 3.
Jim Vejvoda (he/him) is IGN's Assoc. Director of Entertainment Content.

item.title: The Internet Reacts to the Cancelation of Mass Effect 5 and the Death of BioWare.
item.description:
On October 21, EA announced a major restructuring of its development studios and current projects, which included the closure of BioWare and the cancellation of the next Mass Effect game.
This news hit fans like a truck, as many were excitedly waiting for the next installment in the beloved sci-fi role-playing series. BioWare created some of the most beloved and influential RPGs in history over the course of 30 years of existence, but its closure was relegated to just a single paragraph in EA's memo to staff on today's dramatic company changes.
“As we focus on these larger opportunities, we've had a small team at BioWare working on early-development for Mass Effect. We've made the decision not to move forward with this development, which means we’re closing the studio and our Edmonton workspace. BioWare is a legendary studio that helped define the role-playing genre, and we do not take this decision lightly,” Cam Weber, president and chief studios officer, and David Tinson, president and COO, said in the memo.
Needless to say, fans of BioWare games — particularly Mass Effect — were left devastated by this news. On social media, the prevailing sentiment seems to be one of anger and despair, with commenters venting their spleen at EA and the current state of the industry.
“I was so excited for N7 day. I was so excited for the next Mass Effect game. The Mass Effect trilogy is one of my favorite games of all time, and now it’s dead forever. I don’t even know what to think or say, everything feels unreal,” one fan wrote online.
“This is a f**king dagger in my heart. Thank you for being a huge part of my childhood,” another said.
“Please God, PLEASE sell your IPs to another company,” yet another urged. “Don't let the legacy of Mass Effect and Dragon Age die with these last gory gasps. Sell them to other companies that can continue telling the stories they can... Don't let EA hold these settings hostage.”
Prominent members of the video game development community also offered their thoughts. The co-CEO of The Witcher and Cyberpunk developer CD Projekt Red, Michal Nowakowski, weighed in with a statement honoring BioWare for its help and collaboration over the years.
“BioWare has been a massive part of CDPR history. We befriended them when localizing and selling Baldur’s Gate games in Poland, Czech, and Slovakia. And later, they were a great help when lending us their engine for Witcher 1, sharing their wisdom and even giving us a spot at their booth at E3. I had the pleasure to visit them a few times in Edmonton and also host them in our Warsaw office. Very sad for the people affected, but also sad to see a legendary brand go down. Not a great day in the games industry,” he wrote.
Paweł Sasko, associate game director on Cyberpunk 2, said BioWare's Baldur's Gate 1 and 2 "shaped my imagination and the desire to create games." He continued: "I would have never been here without BioWare igniting the fire in my heart. It inspired me, formed me, enriched my imagination, and for that I will be forever grateful. I will always remember you."
inXile boss Brian Fargo, who founded Interplay Entertainment, called it a "sad day indeed." "I remember when BioWare was a small studio that made Shattered Steel for us at Interplay," he said. "We saw the promise in what they could do, and they went on to create Baldur's Gate 1 and 2 and become legendary. A sad day indeed. My thoughts are with everyone there today."
Swen Vincke, boss of Baldur's Gate 3 developer Larian, described BioWare's closure as "not something I ever expected to see."
"Larian and BioWare started their trajectories in the games industry at the same time and BioWare led the way in making RPGs big," he continued. "It's almost unimaginable that we're now entering an era were the name BioWare won't show up anymore when discussing upcoming RPGs. What a loss for all of us.
"Thank you for all the games. Thank you for the many hours of gameplay. Thank you for all the stories . You can be damned proud of what you achieved. I hope you all land well."
Thomas Puha, communications director at Alan Wake and Control developer Remedy, commented: "This was coming but so sad to read. The growing problem for large publishers is that smaller AAA games won’t bring enough money so can’t take the risk on them, but not doing original games? We need those, need new franchises."
Casey Hudson, the former BioWare GM, and director of Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic and the Mass Effect Trilogy, called it "sad news on multiple fronts - for those of us who worked there, for our friends and colleagues at BioWare who are impacted, and for fans who were looking forward to the next Mass Effect adventure.
"I started my career at BioWare and will forever be grateful to the founders, Greg and Ray, for inviting me to join in BioWare's legendary journey. Its legacy will live on through those who were part of it and continue to create games through a passion for unforgettable stories, worlds and characters."
Hudson is now CEO of Arcanaut Studios, which is developing a spiritual successor to KOTOR called Star Wars: Fate of the Old Republic.
BioWare issued a statement of its own on social media, writing: “For more than 30 years, BioWare has been more than a studio. It has been a home for storytellers, developers, and the players who brought our worlds to life. Now, after more than three decades of shared adventures, BioWare is closing and early development on the next Mass Effect project is ending.
“There is nothing easy about writing those words. Our focus right now is on our incredibly talented team who put their hearts into these games, and supporting one another through this transition. What generations of BioWare built together is something to celebrate and remember. These games became so much more because you played them, debated your choices, fell in love with the characters, and made these worlds your own. From all of us at BioWare, thank you for being the most meaningful part of our story.”
Mike Gamble, executive producer of Mass Effect at BioWare, told fans in a social media post: "Your support has meant everything to me over the past 17 years at BioWare."
It’s been a tumultuous year for EA; in August, the company went private in a $55 billion acquisition to an investor group comprised of Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund, Silver Lake, and Affinity Partners. The Financial Times reported that this deal hinged on the hope that AI would “significantly” cut EA’s operating costs, helping the consortium of private investors to better manage the debt they piled onto the game company.
Virginia (she/her) is IGN’s News Editor. With ten years of experience reporting on games and entertainment, she’s got a storied background in the fighting game community, influencer news, and viral online trends. Find her on Twitter at @TheeMissGlaze.

item.title: Disney+ and Hulu have officially picked up a series order of Ryan Murphy’s Glee reboot.
item.description:
Disney+ and Hulu have officially picked up a series order of Ryan Murphy’s Glee reboot.
Murphy first revealed the possibility of a revival in July when he expressed his continued love for the musical series during an interview with People. By September, Murphy announced a finished script, alongside confirmation that he’s already spoken to “about 10 or so” original cast members about returning. While the series order announcement didn't initially reveal any casting news, original cast members like Lea Michele and Heather Morris have since confirmed their involvement.
Gleeks are reacting strongly to the news: “This is the best worst day of my life,” commented one fan. “This is gonna be so bad! I’m so happy and can’t wait,” said another.
Currently gleeking out! https://t.co/ckV50OCQ5s
Why the complicated feelings? Well, in the words of one dedicated Gleek account, “No one is more against this reboot than Gleeks because we all remember its excruciating devolution into insanity.”
While the early seasons of Glee were as critically acclaimed as they were popular, later seasons relied on shock plot lines while struggling to balance a rotating cast of characters. Murphy himself has developed quite the reputation for occasional tone deafness, most recently on display in the true crime Netflix series Monster: The Lizzie Borden Story, with an imagined ending that treats the serial killer series as some kind of MCU multiverse.
Fans’ primary concern, however? Whether we'll see a full reunion of the original cast. One fan argues that “a Glee revival with no cast announced is just a really expensive school choir.”
Some fans have particularly strong opinions on who exactly from the original cast is worth bringing back: “They need to go to Jane Lynch and offer her 1 billion dollars to return because thats the only way this is going to have a chance to work.” Lynch, who played the sardonic cheerleading coach Sue Sylvester, won an Emmy for the role in 2010.
The overwhelming majority of Gleeks have gathered in the comment sections of the announcement to pay tribute to the original cast members, arguing against bringing the series back without them. Per one fan, “Glee without Naya is like earth without water.” Rivera, who played fan-favorite Cheerio Santana Lopez, passed away in a tragic accident in 2020.
Fans also express concern over the reboot potentially “re-evaluating” some of the canon arcs from the original show, particularly the show’s groundbreaking queer relationships. “Don’t touch Brittana,” and “Don’t touch Klaine” are common refrains in the replies.
Still, some fans have a lot to gain from the show’s return. Popular X gimmick account Terri Schuester Updates, which has been consistently active since the show’s cancellation, was quick to recognize what this update means for their own career: “Wait, does this mean I might finally have some actual Terri Schuester updates?”
Other fans are already theorizing about what music will make its way into the reboot, pitching recent breakout popstars like Olivia Rodrigo and Chappell Roan. One particularly popular post jokingly takes a more simplistic stance on the reboot as a whole: “We’re about to get soooo many more songs to say 'they sang this on Glee' to, and that’s really what life is all about.”
Will that be enough reason for fans to tune into the reboot on Disney+? We’ll have to wait and see.
Blythe (she/her) is an Audience Development Coordinator at IGN who spends way too much time in character customization screens and tracking down collectibles.

item.title: EA Sports is working on a new open-world football game, seemingly separate from Madden and College Football.
item.description:
EA Sports is working on a new open-world football game, seemingly separate from Madden and College Football.
In a new letter about EA's future, the company outlined what's on the horizon for its different portfolios. For its sports games, the publisher reaffirmed that it is working on a brand new Fight Night game, which will be EA's first boxing game in well over a decade. However, the more interesting announcement is that EA is working on a new open-world football game that it calls "Project Gridiron."
"We have two new projects in development you’ll hear about over the next few months, including a brand-new, social-first open-world experience for our American Football team that we call 'Project Gridiron,'" said EA. "And we are also in pre-production to bring back a beloved, fan-favorite in Fight Night, leveraging capabilities from our simulation fighting team."
It's unclear if Project Gridiron will have some kind of narrative or if its open-world will be a shared online universe, not unlike NBA 2K. Could this be a more mature and gritty football game, similar to what Fight Night Champion did for that series? It's hard to say right now. Madden briefly dabbled with narrative-driven campaigns in the mid to late 2010s with decent results, but eventually turned its focus back toward a broader career mode for those looking for a progressive single-player experience.
While a new College Football is expected to release next year per previous statements from EA Sports, the existence of Project Gridiron creates a question over whether or not Madden will be benched in favor of this new game.
After all, does anyone have the time, money, or interest in three EA-developed football games in a single year? It's also possible this is a total transformation of the Madden experience, but it sounds like something brand new. It sounds like we won't have to wait too long, as EA noted we will learn more about the game in the "next few months." Perhaps we'll hear about this during The Game Awards or sometime in early 2027, but we'll just have to wait and see.
A recent report also noted that there was some internal concern over the future of College Football, as the rising costs for NIL rights, in addition to other licensing and development expenses, are creating friction. The series' sales have reportedly declined year by year, leading some developers to worry the franchise's return may be relatively short-lived. Perhaps Project Gridiron could replace College Football in the future.
Cade Onder is a freelancer for IGN's news team. He covers all things entertainment, including gaming, film, and more. You can find him on Twitter @Cade_Onder.

item.title: Microsoft is now letting Xbox Insiders stream games by buying cloud playtime without a Game Pass subscription. Here's how much it costs.
item.description:
Microsoft is now letting Xbox Insiders stream games by buying cloud playtime without a Game Pass subscription.
This preview is designed to give Insiders an early look at the new option before it rolls out more broadly next month. Insiders can buy cloud playtime, stream games on supported devices, and share feedback to help us continue improving the experience.
Cloud playtime is available to Insiders at introductory launch pricing:
These cloud playtime packs let you play ad-free, and include shorter wait times, high-quality streaming, and playtime that remains available until it's used, Microsoft said. Insiders can also try cloud gaming for free with ads, as another option for accessing cloud gaming without a Game Pass subscription.
The cloud gaming options for Game Pass subscribers Microsoft announced last month are still set for November. From next month, Game Pass plans will include a set number of cloud gaming hours each month:
Once subscribers use their included hours, they can buy additional cloud playtime through the Xbox Store. Currently, Game Pass subscribers can stream without these monthly hour limits. The change means those who use cloud gaming most via Game Pass will end up having to pay more, although Microsoft said this impacts 4% of Game Pass subscribers.
Cloud gaming has become a focus as the RAMpocalypse makes console gaming increasingly expensive. Strauss Zelnick, boss of Rockstar parent company Take-Two, recently predicted the video game industry will be in “commercial streaming mode” within three years — but for video game streaming to matter, it would have to run GTA 6 just as well as consoles do.
During an investor focused Q&A following the release of Take-Two’s latest financial report, Zelnick was asked for his thoughts on the video game industry as it buckles under the pressure of skyrocketing chip costs, which have forced Sony and Microsoft to raise the price of their consoles and potentially delay the launches of the PlayStation 6 and the next-gen Xbox, codenamed Project Helix.
Zelnick admitted the rising cost of hardware “is not a good thing,” because cheaper hardware means more hardware in people’s hands, which is what software companies desire. But he suggested the advent of video game streaming would go a long way to tackling this problem.
Both Sony and Microsoft are predicted to lean heavily on streaming in the coming years as they contend with the RAMpocalypse. “I just don't have any insight as to what the console manufacturers have planned, but it wouldn't at all surprise me if part of what they plan is streaming,” Zelnick offered.
Just this week, it was reported that the next-gen Xbox may cost as much as $1,800, with a new handheld rumored for next year. New Xbox CEO Asha Sharma has said the spiralling cost of new and existing consoles would require "radically different business models" over the coming generation. She added that the industry had "reached a point where it will be hard to imagine" mass audiences still being able to afford "thousands of dollars" for a new console generation.
The current PS5 and Xbox Series X and S generation of consoles have seen price increases rather than cost savings. Sony itself raised the price of PS5 consoles back in March, blaming “continued pressures in the global economic landscape.” Nintendo has also not been immune, and recently acknowledged it would up the price of Switch 2, just over a year after its arrival. And Valve has bemoaned its struggle to release Steam Machine at the price it had initially hoped, instead having to go for an eye-watering $1,049.

Announced today, Glass Cannon Unplugged, the same studio behind tabletop adaptations of Don’t Starve, Dying Light, and Apex Legends among others, are getting ready to take on the demons of Sanctuary with Diablo: Unbound. Launching a campaign over on Gamefound, Diablo: Unbound is a cooperative dungeon battler for between 1-4 players and features iconic locations and beasts as you level up, and gear out a champion from familiar classes like the Rogue and Barbarian in a quest to take down the dungeon boss.
Diablo®: Unbound is a co-op dungeon battler for 1–4 players. Choose your Class, Dungeon, enemies, and Boss. Fight hordes, hunt loot, and grow stronger!Follow on Gamefound to claim your free, Gamefound Exclusive Treasure Goblin ExpansionLaunching Q1 2027.#boardgames #diablo https://t.co/jZbqbVd4ze
Details are still fairly scarce but already just in the trailer we get some exciting looks at the game from some awesome looking miniatures, various player boards, and even an idea of what the character systems might be. Judging by the map, Unbound looks to have you and your allies facing off against hordes of monsters on a hex grid.
As a big fan of deck builders, seeing that your special abilities and actions are tied to a deck of sorts, has me intrigued. The trailer also showcases a glimpse at the player boards with spots allocated for various armor pieces (with spots open even for gems) including chest, a left and right weapon slot, helm, ring, and necklace. Skills also appear to be taking a page out of the Slay the Spire board game rulebook with skill cards being double-sided with a base side and upgraded side so prepare for sleeving cards, folks.
At a quick glance, fans of boss battlers and dungeon crawling board games, Diablo: Unbound should take notice as this is already teasing some neat systems. For those attending the massive board game convention in Germany, Spiel Essen, this week, you can try out an early build of the game at the Glass Cannon Unplugged booth in Hall I with the campaign planned to launch in Q1 of 2027.
If you're interested in more board games you can play solo, make sure to check out IGN's list of the best single-player tabletop games available now.

item.title: The World of Warcraft Forever beta has been incredibly popular, but just like any other beta, it has to come to an end as the full launch approaches. But Blizzard has extended the beta by a couple of days.
item.description:
The World of Warcraft Forever beta has been incredibly popular, but just like any other, it has to come to an end as the full launch approaches. Thankfully, Blizzard has extended the beta by a couple of days.
WoW Forever's beta was supposed to end yesterday, October 20, but Blizzard announced on X/Twitter that it would be extending the experience by three days. Now the beta will end on October 23 at 10am PT / 1pm ET. After it ends, Blizzard will open name reservations on October 27, which will let you reserve names for three different characters – just make sure they don't break the rules.
It's easy to forget that WoW Forever isn't just out already. Since the beta went live in September, people have been playing it constantly, and just among people playing the beta, there have already been a million characters made. Blizzard devs have even come out and said they were surprised by how many people flocked to the temporary test version of the Classic+ game mode.
Once the full game comes out on November 4, all you'll need to play WoW: Forever is an active subscription or a friend code (though that will just be temporary), so it'll likely be even more popular.
Fans have loved how true the content in the beta so far has stayed to the spirit of the early days of World of Warcraft. Blizzard has made it a point to avoid adding some modern quality-of-life improvements like shared tagging in order to maintain that classic feel. But, rather than strictly avoiding adding anything that was added after WoW's expansions started coming out, Blizzard has included content like the beloved 'Kyle's Gone Missing' quest that takes place in Mulgore.
There have been controversies, too, of course – it wouldn't be WoW without them. Blizzard has had to crack down hard on gold selling, and the company has also been strict with character names. We've even seen people griefing other players by putting down campfires where new players spawn so they die before the intro cinematic finishes.
If you haven't had a chance to dive into the beta yet, you still have a couple days to do so. But keep in mind that any progress you make will be deleted when the game launches in a couple of weeks.
Jackie Thomas is the Senior Tech Editor at IGN and the PC components queen. She's been covering gaming hardware for more than a decade for IGN, TechRadar, Gizmodo, PC Gamer and more. You can follow her @Jackiecobra

item.title: EA has confirmed that DICE and Respawn are working on a new project together, adding more fuel to rumors about Star Wars: Battlefront 3.
item.description:
EA has confirmed that DICE and Respawn are working on a new project together, adding more fuel to rumors about Star Wars: Battlefront 3.
As part of a larger letter about the future of EA, the publisher confirmed that it is working on new Battlefield games. It also noted that in addition to Battlefield, DICE and Respawn are working together on a "future project" that they hope will unlock growth in their shooter portfolio. This follows rumors from earlier this week that the two companies are working together to make Star Wars: Battlefront 3.
"In addition to our future Battlefield titles, we’ll be bringing together our Respawn and DICE studios to collaborate on a future project that will help us achieve that ambition," said EA. "We can’t wait to share more when the time comes."
Variety also corroborated the Battlefront 3 rumors via sources, though nothing was shared on what the game will look like or when it might release. Other rumors recently suggested that Bungie was in the mix to work on Battlefront 3 or perhaps another project in the Star Wars universe, though nothing has been confirmed on that front. Star Wars: Battlefront 3 has been one of the most demanded titles over the last decade.
DICE's second crack at the Star Wars shooter franchise was controversial at launch due to issues with its monetization strategy, but the game itself was praised up and down by fans. It has remained a respected title among Star Wars lovers, and they've frequently rallied together to demand a sequel. Now, it seems like it will happen, though this time with the assistance of Respawn.
The Titanfall and Apex Legends studio has its own experience working on Star Wars through the Jedi games and the recently-released Star Wars Zero Company. Respawn also worked on a canceled Star Wars shooter, rumored to be a Mandalorian game, leaving fans to wonder what could've been. Only time will tell what this new Respawn and DICE game really is, but if it's Battlefront 3, it has serious potential to be something special.
This news came alongside some doom and gloom. EA confirmed that it was canceling the next Mass Effect and shutting down veteran RPG studio BioWare. The news comes after about a decade of commercial and critical misfires from the studio with games like Mass Effect: Andromeda, Anthem, and Dragon Age: The Veilguard.
Cade Onder is a freelancer for IGN's news team. He covers all things entertainment, including gaming, film, and more. You can find him on Twitter @Cade_Onder.

item.title: The top-trending dog and cat names in the United States are dominated by anime characters from franchises such as KPop Demon Hunters and Demon Slayer: Infinity Castle.
item.description:
The top-trending dog and cat names in the United States are dominated by anime characters from franchises such as KPop Demon Hunters and Demon Slayer: Infinity Castle. Characters from The Odyssey and Star Wars: Andor also made the cut.
Names derived from movies and TV shows were the third highest trend in US pet names behind the categories of cottagecore and vintage revival, according to Rover.
The site reveals the top two trending dog names of 2026 are Rumi (KPop Demon Hunters) and Lumi (Lumi and the Great Big Galaxy).
Among dogs, Rover’s top trending movie/TV pet names are Telemachus (The Odyssey), Kleya (Andor), Heathcliff (Wuthering Heights), Fiyero (Wicked: For Good) and Jinu (KPop Demon Hunters).
The top five trending names for cats are Giyu (Demon Slayer: Infinity Castle), Shinobu (Demon Slayer: Infinity Castle), Jinu (KPop Demon Hunters), Derpy (KPop Demon Hunters), and Nessa (Wicked: For Good).
“New names inspired by the big screen this year include Dek (from Predator: Badlands), Reze (from Chainsaw Man: Reze Arc) and Slurp (from Wednesday) for dogs. New for cats are Kamek (from The Super Mario Bros. Movie), Kleya (from Andor) and Makima (from Chainsaw Man: Reze Arc),” according to Rover.
For more anime coverage, find out the latest on the KPop Demon Hunters movie sequel and read up on why Obsession star Inde Navarrette studied Jujutsu Kaisen and Demon Slayer to learn screenwriting.
What’s your pet’s name? Let us know in the comments.
Jim Vejvoda (he/him) is IGN's Assoc. Director of Entertainment Content.
